title: nixos/wastebin: update default POST size to match upstream
reason: Applicable: real wastebin module + wired test (nixos/tests/all-tests.nix at head 5034dd738 contains 'wastebin = runTest ./wastebin.nix;'). Real diff flips WASTEBIN_MAX_BODY_SIZE's own mkOption default (1024 -> 1048576) -- a genuine default-value edit inside a real declaration.

additional_raw_facts_for_reviewer.note: FLAGGING PROMINENTLY, candidate_capability_gap (a real DETECTION gap, distinct from the batch-2/3 rendering-gap finds): check-head.json's own discovered_options list is COMPLETELY EMPTY ([]) for this module -- not just WASTEBIN_MAX_BODY_SIZE, but also enable/package/stateDir/secretFile/settings, every single real mkOption/mkEnableOption/mkPackageOption declaration in the file, none discovered at all. Yet discovered_predicates DOES correctly find `mkIf cfg.enable {` (line 141) -- so the walker parses SOME of this file correctly, just not any declarations. The one thing structurally different about this file versus every other module examined this round: wastebin.nix declares its options via the DOTTED-PATH form `options.services.wastebin = { ... };` (confirmed at line 25), rather than the nested-attrset form `options = { services.wastebin = { ... }; };` every other module in this batch/prior batches uses. This looks like a real, previously-undocumented declaration-walker gap specific to the dotted-attribute-path options-block idiom -- a real, fairly common alternative Nix module-authoring style, not a rare edge case. Not asserting this as confirmed myself; flagging with full evidence for the coordinator/reviewer.
